novelty_flags.label: literature_map / HuberMaric2019
novelty_flags.one_line: The core anchors the cut-polytope claim to “Theorem 3,” but the cited journal article’s iff cut-polytope characterization is Theorem 2 (and no Theorem 3 appears).

soundness_flags.label: symbol rho
soundness_flags.one_line: rho is described as “the square root of the minimum fraction” without specifying the set over which a minimum is taken; define it instead as a free lower-quality parameter, or as ||P_S mu||/||mu|| for a specified nonzero mu.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Statistical Distributions and Applications 6:2 (2019), primary PDF
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The admissible symmetric-Bernoulli correlation vector rho satisfies rho in R(B_n) iff (1-rho)/2 is in CUT_n; the paper has Theorems 1 and 2, not a Theorem 3.
The paper uses exactly balanced sign assignments, represents design risk through Q(sigma)=sum sigma(W)WW', and defines mixed-strategy minimax design for a structured outcome class.
The article frames covariate balance versus robustness in randomized experiments and gives finite-sample MSE control for the Gram--Schmidt Walk design.
The article establishes precision optimality of a matched-pair design among stratified randomization schemes with treatment probability one half.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference 219 (2022), published article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article optimizes a rerandomization threshold using a criterion involving observed and unobserved covariates.
The preprint develops quadratic-form rerandomization results and compares precision implications of different balance matrices.
The preprint optimizes covariate balance through Gaussianized treatment assignments and continuous covariance optimization, rather than the full balanced sign hull.
The work formulates minimax-regret sample selection for randomized trials, an adjacent but distinct design problem.
